h: The Derwent Valley on your doorstep
p: Crich Tramway Village is a real highlight of the Derwent Valley, and there's loads around it to turn a visit into a weekend. Down in the valley, Cromford Mills was where Richard Arkwright built the world's first successful water-powered cotton spinning mill, and the Derwent Valley Mills are now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It's a fascinating place to explore and gives great context to the industrial history you'll see on the trams.

Matlock Bath is the place for a classic day out, with its riverside promenade and the Heights of Abraham, where cable cars carry you up the hillside to caverns and woodland trails with sweeping views. Back in Matlock, Peak Rail runs heritage trains along a stretch of old line towards Rowsley, and the town has a pretty park by the river.

Up on the hill above Crich, Crich Stand is a memorial lighthouse tower to the soldiers of the Sherwood Foresters regiment, and on a clear day the views across Derbyshire are fantastic. It's a lovely stop on the way to or from the trams.

At Crich itself, think about saving the exhibition halls for the middle of the day or when the weather turns, and use the sunny spells for rides out along the line. If anyone in your group is a real tram fan, take time to read the stories behind the vehicles, which come from towns and cities across Britain and abroad. And don't forget a jumper, as the hilltop can be breezier than the valley below.
